item.title: Who is Alaa Abd El-Fattah and why is Keir Starmer under fire
item.description: British-Egyptian activist Alaa Abd El-Fattah has arrived in the UK after Egypt lifted a travel ban. His return follows years of detention and a presidential pardon. Prime Minister Keir Starmer's welcome has drawn criticism due to resurfaced social media posts attributed to Abd El-Fattah, which critics deem violent and antisemitic, prompting calls to review his citizenship.

item.title: ‘Russia wanted Ukraine to succeed,’ says Trump after meeting Zelenskyy — watch his reaction
item.description: President Trump stated Russia desires Ukraine's success, even offering low-cost energy, a remark that visibly surprised and amused President Zelenskyy. The two leaders met at Mar-a-Lago to discuss peace talks, though their underlying relationship dynamics remained unchanged.

item.title: Why Karoline Leavitt’s pregnancy is so rare in American – and world politics
item.description: Karoline Leavitt's quiet announcement of her second pregnancy highlights the unusual intersection of political power and motherhood. While pregnancy is common, its open presence in high office remains rare, exposing how political systems often penalize bodies requiring flexibility. This moment underscores the slow adaptation of institutions to realities millions navigate daily.

item.title: 'Truly repulsive': Tucker Carlson's son Buckley hits back at Ben Shapiro for moving abroad comment
item.description: Buckley Carlson has publicly supported his father, Tucker Carlson, amid a dispute with Ben Shapiro. Shapiro's comments about young Americans unable to afford living in the US have drawn criticism. This exchange follows a history of public disagreements between Shapiro and Tucker Carlson, including past debates and podcast discussions. Buckley Carlson's defense highlights the ongoing tensions within conservative political commentary.

item.title: 'Would you like food—or is that a bribe?': Trump mocks media; jokes about feeding the 'fake news' — Watch video
item.description: Donald Trump hosted Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy at Mar-a-Lago, where a lighthearted moment saw Trump offering lunch to reporters, playfully questioning if it was a bribe. The leaders discussed Zelenskyy's "20-point peace deal proposal," reportedly nearing completion. This meeting followed their earlier, more formal encounter in the Oval Office.

item.title: Empty daycare, misspelled sign and $4m in funding put Minnesota Governor Tim Walz in spotlight — Here's what we know about fraud
item.description: A viral video highlighted a Minneapolis daycare center, Quality Learning Center, receiving $4 million in state funding despite appearing inactive and misspelling its name. This incident has intensified criticism of Governor Tim Walz amid a larger scandal involving alleged fraud in Minnesota's social service programs, prompting calls for accountability from Republican lawmakers and national figures.

item.title: Twitch streamer Cloakzy raises concerns over viewbotting after spotting unknown high viewership channels
item.description: Popular Twitch streamer Cloakzy has highlighted a worrying trend. He observes many new streamers suddenly attracting huge viewer numbers, sparking questions about viewbotting. This comes as Twitch has been trying to combat fake viewership. Cloakzy's comments suggest the problem may still be prevalent, impacting fair competition for legitimate content creators on the platform.

item.title: Watch: Two helicopters collide mid-air and crash in US; video shows thick smoke billowing from ground

item.title: Over 10,000 people displaced in 3 days in Sudan: UN
item.description: Violence in western and southern Sudan displaced more than 10,000 people within a three-day period this week, according to figures released by the United Nations' migration agency on Sunday. Between December 25 and 26, attacks on the villages of Um Baru and Kernoi near Sudan's western border with Chad displaced more than 7,000 people, according to the International Organization for Migration.

item.title: Indian-origin startup CEO claims his company is being extorted for $3 million: 'Illegally obtained confidential information'
item.description: Giga, an AI startup, is targeted by an extortion scheme. Individuals allegedly obtained confidential data and demand $3 million in cryptocurrency. They threaten to release manipulated information and false allegations. This incident follows previous accusations of unethical practices by former employees. The company denies wrongdoing, attributing the claims to a smear campaign after a recent funding round. Read more here!

item.title: 'Canadians are dying': Mark Carney's $2.5 billion aid to Ukraine draws backlash online
item.description: Canada pledged an additional $2.5 billion in aid to Ukraine, with much of it channeled through international financial institutions. This significant contribution, part of broader global support, has sparked outrage among Canadians online. Critics argue the funds should prioritize domestic needs like healthcare, citing instances of suffering citizens while vast sums are sent abroad.

item.title: 'About 90% ready': Trump-Zelenskyy Florida meet on Ukraine peace deal amid renewed Russian attacks - what's on agenda
item.description: US President Trump is set to meet Ukrainian counterpart Zelenskyy at Mar-a-Lago to discuss a peace proposal amid escalating Russian attacks. Zelenskyy seeks strong support and pressure on Moscow, emphasising security guarantees and territorial issues. While both leaders aim for peace, significant hurdles remain regarding Russia's aggression and territorial gains.
